scope: Historical 2020-2024 landed import costs and domestic-resource export revenues for coal and crude oil
intended_behavior: Domestic extraction may serve the domestic raw-fuel pool or an optional export sink. Imports remain open and can serve only the domestic pool. Consistent external border prices determine the routing endogenously; no production, trade volume, share or dispatch outcome is imposed.

exogenous_economic_drivers: Philippine landed coal import unit value
Philippine landed crude import unit value
master_rule_classification.assessment: Changing external prices calibrates an underlying economic driver and does not force an endogenous trade outcome. Observed trade quantities are not used in TAL, TAU, shares or equalities.

technology_classification.PHL_PRO_IMP_COAL: open import backstop producing the existing raw-coal pool; only mode 1 has nonzero output
technology_classification.PHL_PRO_EXP_COAL: optional consume-only accounting sink for source-tagged domestic coal
technology_classification.PHL_PRO_IMP_OIL: open import backstop producing the existing raw-crude pool; only mode 1 has nonzero output
technology_classification.PHL_PRO_EXP_OIL: optional consume-only accounting sink for source-tagged Galoc crude

equation_mapping.objective_effect: RateOfActivity * YearSplit * VariableCost enters the discounted objective directly
equation_mapping.accounting_equation: OC1_OperatingCostsVariable equates the timeslice activity-cost sum to AnnualVariableOperatingCost
equation_mapping.scenario_behavior: SC_3hgjb, SC_huc7i and SC_w03qj retain null VC cells and inherit SC_0
equation_mapping.sign_convention: landed import cost is positive; external export revenue is stored as negative variable cost

units_and_conversions.oil_export_formula: USD per barrel / 6.119 GJ per barrel

coal_import.basis: Philippine customs CIF value divided by reported coal mass

coal_export.basis: Philippine customs FOB value divided by reported coal mass

oil_import.basis: DOE crude import bill divided by DOE crude import volume; one internally consistent landed-cost series

2024.source_report: DOE FY2024; crude bill = 16884.9 total - 12686.3 products

oil_export.basis: Galoc realized crude selling price; aggregate customs HS 2709 was rejected because it combines crude and condensate

rejected_calculation.method: PSA/customs aggregate HS 2709 value divided by DOE crude volume
rejected_calculation.reason: The numerator and denominator came from different statistical scopes. HS 2709 also includes condensate, while DOE reports crude supply and its bill directly. The mixed series understated 2021-2022 landed crude cost and incorrectly implied that Galoc export revenue exceeded landed import cost in 2022.
rejected_calculation.action: No mixed-source value was written to model source. DOE bill/volume replaced it before candidate creation.

future_path.2025_onward: unchanged from the accepted live case
future_path.coal: 2025 SMPC realized value; World Bank 2026-2027 quality-adjusted forecast; 2027 held thereafter
future_path.oil: World Bank Brent 2025-2027; 2027 held thereafter; immaterial after physical Galoc cessation

deterministic_price_spreads.definition: landed import cost minus export revenue magnitude; positive means export-and-replace is uneconomic before domestic bridge/handling costs

known_structural_limitations: A single interchangeable coal pool cannot reproduce simultaneous exports of lower-grade/local coal and imports of plant-compatible grades.
A single interchangeable crude pool cannot reproduce Galoc exports alongside imports of different refinery-compatible crude when landed imports cost more than Galoc export revenue.
Any resulting zero export is a disclosed validation gap, not a target imposed by this change.
